M1.reason: The brief asks for a forklift with a driver in its seat, which has a mast, forks, a driver's overhead guard, wheels and a counterweight. In every one of the ten views (sides.png) the outline is a plain rectangular block: front, back, left, right, top, below and the four isometric views all show the same closed box with no mast, forks, guard, seat or wheels breaking the silhouette.

M2.reason: Measured size is 186.6 x 60 x 113 against the brief's 187 long, 60 wide and 113 high (sizeOff 0.003), so each dimension is within 15% of the brief's size. The side views in sides.png confirm the proportions.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, none present: two forks, the mast and its uprights, the lift carriage, the overhead guard and its posts, the seat, the driver, the steering wheel, the front and rear wheels, the counterweight. The model is one solid block with no components, so the parts are missing.

M4.reason: The brief names no colour, so the grey metal body is not wrong, but the materials it implies are absent: the rubber tyres, the driver's cloth and skin and the seat are missing, and the one flat grey material covers the whole block. Only one region exists, and it is a placeholder grey.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no specific markings, but an industrial forklift would carry some detail (a guard's bars, a mast's channels, panel lines or a warning mark). The only surface detail is a faint noise grain over the faces and bevelled edges in sides.png and lineup.png (C); nothing else is there.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the rubric directs, since M6 is measured apart by the line-up test: the asset (lineup C) was not picked as the non-Valve model in any of the four readings (the picks were B, B, B, C against the asset's positions C, C, A, B), so the test was passed. Visually, a grey box in the line-up beside the globe, the snail-like fungus and the barnacle-like leg is not a forklift, so my own impression disagrees with the line-up result; the score follows the measured test.

M7.reason: The block stands upright on its base in the front, side and below views, so the placement is plausible. A forklift has a front (the mast and forks) and a back (the counterweight and seat); the box has no identifiable front, so the facing cannot be the original's. Clearly off, so 1.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks pass with no errors. Triangles are 12, under the 352 limit (twice Half-Life's median of 176 for props of this kind, which is more than the three-quarter mark of 296). The views show a closed box with no open faces, inside-out faces or floating parts.
